newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoro Islands secessionist leaders released.
newsitem.headline: Comoro Islands secessionist leaders released.

text.p: Authorities in the Indian Ocean Comoro Islands have released two leaders of a secessionist movement on Anjouan island after they were briefly detained, witnesses said.
Retired army chief Commander Zaki Nassor, 73, and charismatic preacher Foundi Abdallah Ibrahim, 75, were detained by gendarmes on the main Grand Comoro island on Wednesday.
The army on Anjouan used hand grenades on Monday to bring down a French flag hoisted by secessionists in a gesture of defiance.

"I told them (gendarmes) that if it was me who had raised the French flag I would have done it openly and not in hiding, but I also let them know that we are determined to defend the interests of Anjouan at all costs," Ibrahim told Reuters after his release.

The archipelego, with a population of 190,000, became independent from France in 1975 but some islanders appear to want to return to the French fold, saying life in the Comoros is reduced by poverty, corruption and a succession of coups.
Tension is high on Anjouan where clashes between the army and residents last March caused several deaths and led to many arrests.
